_README: RM MODULE TOOLS TEMPLATE
This file defines the TOOLS your module injects: hollow item forms
whose material comes from whatever they are made of. Reactions take
a tool with a TOOL reagent's tool_id and make one with a product's
subtype, both naming its full ID.
HOW TO USE THIS FILE:
1. Copy it into your mod's data/ folder.
2. Rename it to <yourmod>_tools.json.
3. Change the module block below to your own prefix.
4. Replace the tools array with your own content.
5. Hand it to RM from your listener as tools_json, the way
rm-module-template-advanced.lua hands over its files.
THE UNDERSCORE CONVENTION:
Any key starting with an underscore is documentation. RM's engine
reads only the keys it knows about, so _README and _comment are
ignored at load time. Keep them, edit them, or delete them.
LEAVING A FIELD OUT:
RM builds each tool as a new, empty itemdef. A field you leave out
is not written, so it keeps that empty default. Nothing comes from
another tool unless graphics names a donor.
PREFIXING:
You write key. The tool's ID is module.prefix .. key: key CRUCIBLE
under prefix MYMOD_ becomes MYMOD_CRUCIBLE. Reactions name it by
that full ID.
VALIDATION:
RM checks each tool on its own. A bad entry is left out and named
in the log, and the rest are injected. A reaction whose product
names a left-out tool by subtype is left out with it.
CHECK RM'S CATALOG FIRST:
RM already carries dust, gravel, heaps, sawdust, bark, scrap,
cullet and crust. Ask for those with requires in your
module block instead of defining your own (guide section 9).
FULL FIELD DOCUMENTATION:
RM_MODULE_ENGINE_README.md, section 7.1.

module._comment: Identity block. prefix is required and must be the prefix your other files use: RM injects your tools under the module's prefix. name and depends_on are read from here only when the module has no materials or reactions file.
module.name: RM Module Template
module._comment_requires: Optional. RM catalog forms your module uses (guide section 9). Gathered from every file's module block, so it may sit here or in any other.

tools._comment: REFERENCE ENTRY. Every field the schema accepts. Copy this one when you want to see the whole surface, then delete the lines you do not need.
tools._comment_key: Required. Uppercase, no spaces. The tool's ID is prefix + key.
tools._comment_names: name is required. name_plural is optional to RM, but preflight requires it and items read wrong without it. adjective is optional.
tools.name: crucible
tools._comment_size: Optional. size is the itemdef's size. material_size is the material it takes to make, 3 to a bar: RM's melting pays a melted tool back on it.
tools._comment_capacity: Optional. What the tool holds as a container (the itemdef's container_capacity). 0 for a tool that holds nothing.
tools._comment_tile: Optional. ASCII mode only: the character code of the tool's tile. The graphical game draws the sprite from graphics below.
tools._comment_flags: Optional. DF's tool flags by name, each true or false, as a tool raw declares them: furniture, inverted_tile, no_default_job, incomplete_item, unimprovable, no_default_improvements, hard_mat, metal_mat, soft_mat, stone_mat, wood_mat, sheet_mat, metal_weapon_mat. A name not in that list is ignored.
tools._comment_tool_use: Optional. df.tool_uses names (guide Appendix B). A HAS_<USE> reagent finds the tool by these. An unknown name is logged and skipped.
tools._comment_graphics: Optional. The tool's sprite. donor copies every sprite field of another tool, named as a source such as TOOL:ITEM_TOOL_JUG. fields writes named itemdef sprite fields (texpos_item, texpos_stone and the rest) one by one, each a source string or a table { donor, offset, fill }. Sources are listed in guide section 4.7; a FILE path is relative to your data folder. See the second entry for fields.
tools._comment_tint: Optional. The name of art registered with refinish-sprite-art. RM then draws the tool from that art in each material's own colour. Leave it out and the sprite is drawn as DF draws it.
tools._comment_stack: Optional, default false. True: when a reaction makes this tool, RM merges the new items into one stack per material.

tools._comment: EXAMPLE. A stacking form drawn from your own sheet: column 0, row 0 of data/images/my_module_sheet.png, a sheet 4 tiles wide.
tools.name: fines
